title: Stories Worth Telling
goals: Contrast simple and continuous verbs in the present, present perfect and past to talk about routines, temporary situations and experiences.
Use verb + -ing and verb + to + verb correctly (decide to, finish doing, end up doing...).
Tell how remember, stop and try change in meaning depending on whether -ing or to follows.
Tell an anecdote with a clear thread: general time, a particular moment, what happened and an ending.
Add emphasis to key moments with the dramatic present and with this / these.
Write an anecdote and an email about your current life using the vocabulary of the unit.

learn.title: Simple and continuous verbs (review)
learn.html:
Simple verbs describe completed actions, habits or permanent situations. Continuous verbs describe actions in progress or temporary situations. Choosing correctly changes the meaning, not just the form.

TenseSimpleContinuous
PresentI listen to jazz a lot. (habit, permanent)I'm listening to a lot of jazz these days. (temporary)
Present perfectI've never lived abroad. (experience, result)I've been living here for five years. (still happening)
PastI went home and had a party. (completed action)I was sitting on a bus at nine. (action in progress, sometimes interrupted)
  • Typical expressions with the continuous: currently, these days, lately, right now, at this time yesterday.
  • State verbs (know, like, love, want, need, belong, understand) are almost never used in the continuous: I know her, not I'm knowing her.
  • With for / since and a situation that continues, use the present perfect (simple or continuous), not the present.

watch.wrong: I'm knowing her since high school.
watch.right: I've known her since high school.
watch.why: Know is a state verb, and with since we use the present perfect.

watch.right: I've been living in Puebla since 2019.
watch.why: A situation that started in the past and is still going on: present perfect.

watch.wrong: I watched TV when the phone rang.
watch.right: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
watch.why: A long action that was interrupted goes in the past continuous.

watch.wrong: I've been finishing the report. Here it is.
watch.right: I've finished the report. Here it is.
watch.why: If the result already exists, use the simple form, not the continuous.

learn.title: Verb + -ing or to + verb
learn.html:
When a main verb needs another verb, the second one can take -ing or to + infinitive. It depends on the first verb, so these verbs are best learned in groups.

PatternVerbsExample
verb + -ingconsider, finish, imagine, miss, (not) mind, spend time, enjoy, avoidI finished writing the report.
verb + particle/preposition + -ingend up, keep on, plan on, think aboutWe ended up sleeping in the car.
verb + to + verbagree, decide, expect, happen, intend, offer, seemThey agreed to pay for the repairs.
-ing or to, same meaningbegin, start, continue, like, love, hate, botherIt began raining. / It began to rain.

After a preposition (about, on, of, without) you always use -ing: I'm thinking about moving. Speakers of Spanish tend to use the infinitive in almost every case, and that is where many mistakes come from.

watch.why: Decide is followed by to + verb.

watch.wrong: We ended up to take a taxi.
watch.right: We ended up taking a taxi.

learn.title: remember, stop and try: -ing or to
learn.html:
With three key verbs, the meaning changes depending on the form that follows.

Verb+ -ing+ to + verb
rememberI remember locking the door. (I recall doing it)Remember to lock the door. (don't forget to do it)
stopI stopped talking to him. (we no longer talk)I stopped to talk to him. (I stopped in order to talk to him)
tryTry restarting the router. (experiment, see if it works)I tried to lift the box. (I made the effort)

Practical rule: -ing looks at something that already happened or at an experiment; to looks at a purpose or an effort.

watch.wrong: I stopped to smoke last year.
watch.why: Giving up a habit is expressed as stop + -ing.

watch.wrong: Remember closing the windows when you leave.
watch.right: Remember to close the windows when you leave.
watch.why: For a task you still have to do, use remember to.

watch.wrong: I tried to eat sushi once and I loved it.
watch.right: I tried eating sushi once and I loved it.
watch.why: Trying something as an experiment: try + -ing.

watch.wrong: She stopped to work in 2020 (she retired).

learn.title: Telling stories: the dramatic present and this / these
learn.html:
When telling an anecdote in conversation, almost everything is in the past, but at the key moments you can switch to the present to make them more vivid. Also, this / these highlight important people, places or things in the story, even if the listener doesn't know them yet.

ResourceExample
Past for the backgroundThere were all these trees around us, and we were completely lost.
Present for the key momentAnd we're thinking, "Oh, no." And we're both getting scared.
this / these for emphasisWe were on this trail... There were all these trees...
Story connectorsone day, all of a sudden, on the day of the show, in case anything happens

To write an anecdote, follow four steps: (1) set the general time or place, (2) mark the particular moment, (3) tell what happened, (4) close the story and, if you can, connect it to the present.

watch.wrong: We were on these trail in the middle of nowhere.
watch.right: We were on this trail in the middle of nowhere.

watch.wrong: There were this trees around us.
watch.right: There were all these trees around us.
watch.why: Plural: these, and all emphasizes the quantity.

watch.wrong: All of sudden, the lights went out.
watch.right: All of a sudden, the lights went out.
watch.why: The full expression is all of a sudden.

watch.wrong: Yesterday I'm walking home and I see an old friend.
watch.right: Yesterday I was walking home and I saw an old friend.
watch.why: Don't mix the present with a past time marker like yesterday when you open the story.

learn.title: Functions: opening, telling and closing a story
learn.html:
• When I was in high school, ... / A few years ago, ... — set the general time.
  • One day, ... / On the day of the speech, ... — move to the particular moment.
  • All of a sudden, ... — introduce a surprise.
  • And we're thinking, "Oh, no." — dramatic present at the key moment.
  • It's a long story! — warn that what follows is long or complicated.
  • I wasn't planning on ... / I ended up ... — say that something was not planned and how it ended.
  • It was a big challenge, but it helped me become ... — close the story and connect it to the present.
  • Should I bother (to) apply? — ask whether the effort is worth it.

write.prompt: Write an anecdote of 180 to 250 words about a trip, a difficult day or a surprise. Follow these steps: (1) set the general time, (2) mark the particular moment with one day / on the day of, (3) tell what happened using past continuous for the background and past simple for the actions, and switch to the present at a key moment, (4) close the story and connect it to your life today. Possible opening: When I was ...
checklist: Between 180 and 250 words
General time, particular moment, event and ending
Past continuous for the background and past simple for the actions
At least three verbs with -ing or to + verb, used correctly (ended up, decided to, finished...)
A key moment in the present and at least one this / these
At least three connectors (one day, all of a sudden, in case...)
A closing sentence that connects the story to the present
write.model:
When I was twenty, I traveled alone to Puebla for the first time. It was a rainy day in October, and I was carrying a heavy bag. One day earlier, my mother had told me not to forget my umbrella, but I did not listen.

On the day of the trip, I was waiting at the bus station when I realized that my wallet was missing. I remembered leaving it on the kitchen table, but I could not go back. I decided to call my cousin, who lived near the station. All of a sudden, my phone rang, and it was her!

So here I am, standing in the rain, and I hear her voice: "Where are you? I'm already at the station!" I start laughing, because she is right behind me. This is the moment I will never forget. She pays for my ticket, and we hug.

We ended up spending the whole weekend together. While we were walking through the city, it started to pour, so we stopped to buy two umbrellas in case it rained again. Finally, I finished the trip without any other problem.

Since then, I always check my bag before leaving, and I try to stay calm when things go wrong. These small mistakes taught me that a bad start does not have to ruin a whole trip.

write.prompt: Write an email of 180 to 250 words to a friend who lives in another country. Tell them what you are doing these days, what you have been doing lately (currently, lately), your plans for this year (planning on, intend to) and a short recent anecdote. End with two questions for them.
targets: planning on / intend to / decide to
checklist: Between 180 and 250 words
Contrast between the simple present (habits) and the continuous (temporary)
At least two sentences with the present perfect continuous (for / since / lately)
At least three verbs with -ing or to + verb, used correctly
A short anecdote in the simple past and past continuous
Email greeting and sign-off, and two questions for your friend
write.model:
Hi Lucía,

How are things in Toronto? I hope you are doing well. Here, life is busy as usual. I usually get up at six and go to work by train, but this month I'm working from home because the office is being painted. Currently I'm also taking a photography course on Saturdays.

Lately I have been thinking a lot about my future. I have been saving money since January, and I have been looking at apartments for rent. I'm planning on moving to a new place later this year, and I intend to live closer to the city center. I have also decided to learn how to cook, so I have been trying new recipes every weekend. Some of them have been a disaster!

Let me tell you a funny story. Last Sunday I was making a cake when the smoke alarm went off. I was talking on the phone with my mom, so I forgot about the oven. By the time I noticed, the kitchen was full of smoke, and my neighbor was knocking on the door. We laughed about it later.

I would love to hear your news. Have you been traveling much lately? And are you thinking about coming to Mexico this year?

Write soon!

Love,
Elena

reading.title: The Wrong Trail
reading.intro: Read the story of a weekend that did not go as planned, then answer the questions.
paragraphs: Last October, my friend Daniela and I decided to spend a long weekend in the mountains outside Oaxaca. I had been working twelve hours a day for months, and I was thrilled to leave the city. We were planning on hiking for a few hours on Saturday morning and driving home on Sunday. Nobody expected it to become the most memorable trip of our lives.

We started early. The weather was perfect, and we kept on walking longer than we intended. Around noon, Daniela stopped to take a photo of a tiny waterfall, and I remember thinking how peaceful everything was. Then we ended up following a narrow path that did not appear on our map. We should have turned back, but we were enjoying ourselves too much, and we didn't mind getting a little lost.

By four o'clock the sky was getting dark, and we were both getting scared. There were all these tall trees around us, and every path looked the same. I'm trying to stay calm, but my heart is pounding. Daniela is checking her phone, and there is no signal. All of a sudden, we hear a bell. A farmer is walking toward us with two goats, and he's smiling as if this were completely normal.

The farmer, Don Aurelio, offered to walk with us to his village. He didn't talk much, but he seemed to know every rock on the mountain. We stuck together and followed him in silence. When we finally arrived, his wife let us in and gave us hot chocolate and fresh tortillas. The village had no hotel, so we slept in a small room above the kitchen. Before going to bed I tried calling my mother, but there was still no signal, so I wrote her a long message and promised myself I would send it in the morning.

At dawn, the whole family was already awake. His grandchildren were feeding the chickens, and they looked at us as if we were famous explorers. We had breakfast, and Don Aurelio refused to accept any money, but he agreed to let us pay for the tortillas. Then he drove us back to our car in his old truck, and we spent the whole ride laughing about our mistake.

These days I'm working fewer hours, and I have been trying to take more long weekends off. Daniela is currently planning another trip, but this time we're bringing a paper map, a charger and, in case anything happens, a whistle. I never forgot to thank that farmer. I still remember hearing that bell, and I think about it whenever I feel I cannot get through a difficult day.

glossary.def: very excited and happy about something
a narrow path, often in the mountains or in the forest
the connection that lets a phone make calls or use the internet
beating very fast and strongly (said of the heart)
a farm animal with horns that gives milk
to stay close to each other so nobody gets separated
the early morning, when the sun starts to rise
a small device you blow to make a loud sound, often to get attention or for help

listening.title: It's a long story
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two coworkers. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Mateo, you look tired. What happened?
Oh, it's a long story. I'm currently working two jobs, and lately I've been sleeping about five hours a night.
That sounds hard. Is that why you were late yesterday?
Partly. Yesterday I was riding the bus to the office, and I was reading an email. I stopped looking out of the window.
Then I look up, and we're on this highway, and all these buildings are different. I ended up in the next town!
No way! Did you try calling your boss?
I tried calling her, but my battery was dead. I remember thinking, why didn't I charge my phone?
I got off, and a kind man offered to give me a ride to the station. I finished my trip by train.
I'm glad it worked out. Will you keep on taking the bus?
Honestly, I'm considering buying a bike. At least I can't fall asleep on a bike!
